A.question: Are opportunities for PFL legislative-event scoring temporally concentrated beyond competent calendar-aware baselines, in UK House Commons divisions in calendar year 2025?
A.unit: calendar ISO week and voting day
A.population: UK Commons official recorded divisions dated 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31
A.exposure: Parliament division availability, no individual politician assessment
A.outcome: number of divisions per week; per vote-day
A.estimand: variance/mean of weekly counts, concentration top quartile weeks, and Poisson/negative-binomial versus baseline
A.interference: divisions on same date are dependent and may concern same legislative matter

B.h1: Substantial clustering and concentration of weekly opportunities beyond equal-rate model
B.h2: Clustering explained by parliamentary sitting calendar and number of vote days
B.h0: No material excess heterogeneity over weekday opportunity baseline

C.filter: 2025 year, no member query, all pages
C.completeness: API total count; dedupe divisionId; verify years and dates and paging
baselines: homogeneous weekly Poisson count with same mean
weekday-opportunity model with number of observed vote days (endogenous descriptive control)
C.guardrail: No causal or person-activity inference; if truncated or inaccessible STOP_LOCAL
C.novelty: PFL exposure calibration rather than claim of new institutional effect

D.rights: Open Parliament Licence v3 attributed; exclude personal data and names
D.qa: original API JSON return preferred, store only aggregated dates, IDs, counts, source hashes where obtainable
